content.title: About
content.content: Canned chili with meat is a ready‑to‑eat product consisting of a thick, spicy tomato‑based sauce with beans and pieces of beef (or pork). Made according to a traditional recipe, it is sealed in a glass or metal jar and can be served after heating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: In the United States chili is considered a classic comfort food and is often served with rice, potatoes or bread.
The tomatoes used in the sauce are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Traditional seasoning includes cumin, paprika, oregano and chili powder, giving the dish its characteristic aroma.
Canning preserves flavor and nutrients for up to 2‑3 years without added preservatives.
In many countries chili with meat is a popular quick lunch for travelers and office workers.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Lycopene and vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes supply lycopene and vitamin C, supporting immunity and protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Beans add soluble and insoluble fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Spices with antimicrobial properties
items.content: Cumin and chili powder have mild antimicrobial and anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain a lot of salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Spicy heat
items.content: The chili level may be too hot for children or individuals with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to beef or pork.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Certain brands use preservatives such as sodium benzoate; choose additive‑free versions if you are sensitive.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the jar in the microwave or on the stove until boiling, serve over rice, mashed potatoes, toast, or use as a filling for tacos. Garnish with fresh herbs, sour cream, or shredded cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3‑4 days, always reheating thoroughly.

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate Milk NFS is a ready‑to‑drink beverage made by blending whole cow’s milk with cocoa powder, sugar, and flavorings. Its nutritional profile is similar to regular milk, enriched with a chocolate taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first mass production of chocolate milk began in the United States in the early 20th century.
In Russia, chocolate milk became popular in the 1990s thanks to imported brands.
Most ready‑to‑drink versions contain 2‑5 % cocoa solids.
Chocolate milk is often used in children’s nutrition as a source of calcium and quick energy.
Some countries fortify it with vitamin D to enhance calcium absorption.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The milk base provides a high level of calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B2 and B12 support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Milk proteins contribute to growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Sugar and a modest amount of fat give a quick source of energy, useful for children and active individuals.

items.title: Mood enhancer
items.content: Cocoa contains theobromine and small amounts of phenylethylamine, which may help improve mood.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High sugar levels can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance should choose lactose‑free versions or limit consumption.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey protein requires complete avoidance of the product.

items.title: Caffeine and theobromine
items.content: Although present in small amounts, sensitive individuals may experience mild stimulation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chocolate milk can be enjoyed cold as a refreshing drink, used in smoothies, as a base for dessert sauces, or added to cereals and oatmeal for flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. After opening, consume within 3‑5 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may change.

content.title: About
content.content: Whipped cream is a light, airy dessert topping made by beating high‑fat dairy cream (typically 30‑36 % milk fat). The beating process creates a stable emulsion that holds air bubbles, giving the cream a soft, fluffy texture. It is commonly used to top cakes, pastries, hot drinks, and fresh fruit.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally whipped cream was made by hand, but today most producers use mixers and stabilizers.
Stabilizers such as gelatin, starch, or commercial food stabilizers are often added to improve holding power.
Whipped cream can be flavored with vanilla, chocolate, caramel, or fruit purées.
In the United States, aerosol “spray” whipped cream is popular; nitrogen or nitrous oxide propels the cream and helps it keep its shape.
Cream used for whipping must contain at least 30 % fat; lower‑fat creams do not form a stable foam.

items.title: Source of Vitamin A
items.content: Cream is rich in vitamin A, which supports vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Contains Vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D in cream aids calcium absorption and promotes bone health.

items.title: Contains Fat‑Soluble Vitamins
items.content: Vitamins E and K present in cream have antioxidant and blood‑clotting benefits.

items.title: Calcium and Phosphorus
items.content: These minerals are important for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Energy Dense
items.content: The fat in cream provides a quick source of energy, useful during high‑intensity activities.

items.title: High Fat and Calorie Content
items.content: Large servings can contribute to weight gain and raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Lactose Intolerance
items.content: People who are lactose intolerant may experience digestive discomfort after consuming cream.

items.title: Milk Protein Allergy
items.content: Allergic reactions to casein or whey can occur in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Saturated Fat
items.content: Excessive intake of saturated fat is linked to increased cardiovascular risk.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve whipped cream over berries, ice cream, hot chocolate, pancakes, and cakes. It can be folded into mousses, custards, and sauces, or added to coffee and cocktails for a silky, airy finish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep whipped cream refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in a sealed container and use within 3‑5 days. If the cream is already whipped, store it in an airtight bowl to prevent it from absorbing other odors. Discard if it develops a sour smell or off‑color.

content.title: About
content.content: Fried broccoli is broccoli quickly sautéed in a small amount of oil until it develops a golden crust. The cooking method retains most of the vitamins and minerals while giving the vegetable a crunchy texture and rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli belongs to the cruciferous family and is rich in glucosinolates, compounds with antioxidant properties.
Quick frying preserves more vitamin C than prolonged boiling.
Fried broccoli is a common side dish in Asian cuisine, often tossed with soy sauce and garlic.
A popular variation is "tempura broccoli," where florets are coated in batter before frying.
Broccoli is considered a "superfood" due to its high fiber and phytonutrient content.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients such as sulforaphane help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in broccoli contribute to normal blood pressure.

items.title: Cruciferous allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to broccoli.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Broccoli contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Added fat from frying
items.content: Using excessive oil can make the dish calorie‑dense.

items.title: Possible pesticide residues
items.content: Improperly washed broccoli may retain pesticide residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried broccoli can be served as a side dish, tossed into salads, noodle or rice dishes. Season with soy sauce, lemon juice, garlic, or your favorite spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh broccoli in a sealed container in the refrigerator for 3–5 days. Cooked fried broccoli should be consumed within 1–2 days, kept refrigerated.

content.title: About
content.content: Enfamil Nutramigen is a hypoallergenic infant formula based on extensively hydrolyzed cow’s milk protein, designed for infants with suspected food allergy or lactose intolerance. The ready‑to‑feed format provides precise dosing and convenience without any preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula contains fully hydrolyzed protein, reducing the risk of allergic reactions.
Specifically developed for newborns and infants at high risk of atopy.
Includes prebiotic fibers (FOS) to support a healthy gut microbiome.
No water addition required, minimizing contamination risk.
Each container carries a batch‑tracking barcode for traceability and expiration monitoring.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Hydrolyzed protein and prebiotics help develop the infant’s immune system, especially in those prone to allergies.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Extensively hydrolyzed protein is broken down more quickly in the gastrointestinal tract, reducing digestive load.

items.title: Balanced nutrition
items.content: The formula provides essential vitamins, minerals, and DHA for brain and eye development.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Suitable for infants with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Convenient use
items.content: Ready‑to‑feed eliminates the need for bottle sterilization and measuring volumes.

items.title: Cow‑milk protein allergy
items.content: Although the protein is hydrolyzed, some infants may still react to residual peptide fragments.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The formula contains a small amount of lactose; infants with complete intolerance should be monitored by a pediatrician.

items.title: Post‑opening storage
items.content: Once opened, the product should be used within 48 hours and kept refrigerated.

items.title: Feeding guidance
items.content: Do not replace breast milk entirely without pediatric advice.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Prepare a clean bottle, open the container and feed the ready‑to‑feed formula directly to the baby. If desired, warm to body temperature (about 37 °C) and test on the wrist. Do not leave the formula at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened containers in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, refrigerate and use within 48 hours. Discard if the product develops an off‑odor, color change, or unusual taste.

content.title: About
content.content: Leeks (Allium ampeloprasum var. porrum) are a perennial vegetable from the onion family. The plant produces long, flat leaves that form a thick, white "stem". The flavor is mild, slightly sweet, and aromatic. Leeks are eaten raw, boiled, roasted, and are a staple in soups, salads, and stews.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Leeks belong to the same species group as common onion, garlic, and shallots.
In ancient Rome, leeks were a symbol of strength and were used for medicinal purposes.
The leek stalk is made of multiple layered leaves that create its characteristic tube shape.
In Russia, leeks are traditionally grown in open fields and greenhouses, while in Japan they are often featured in the dish "nama-edama".
Leeks contain more vitamin K than most other vegetables.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K plays a key role in blood clotting and supports bone health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and sulfur compounds help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy to alliums
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to leeks, including itching, swelling, or gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: People with sensitive stomachs or irritable bowel syndrome may experience gas and bloating after eating leeks.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Leeks contain small amounts of oxalates, which can be a concern for those prone to kidney stones.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Leeks can be added to soups, stews, casseroles, salads, and used as a filling for pies. The white part of the stalk is usually cooked, while the green leaves can be added to stocks or used as a garnish. Before cooking, rinse thoroughly to remove sand trapped between the layers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leeks in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a plastic bag or placed in a container with a small amount of moisture. When stored properly, they stay fresh for up to two weeks. Keep them away from fruit, as they can accelerate fruit spoilage.
